Frozen at 2026-11-22T23:53:21.9439674Z UTC on November 22, 2026. No packet, capture manifest, source, contract, or previous review read before this note.

Media reviewed
- Published Lens. All 16 Journal ready, Lens ready, inspected and returned checkpoint PNGs, at desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 in normal and reduced motion. Sampled 19, 19, 19, and 18 main-page JPEG frames in timeline order across their four Playwright traces. The Lens is clearly a modal over the same Journal, titled A message between worlds. The camera path is explicitly disabled here and Guided View immediately gives the Captain's note with the northern-light clue. The Inspect action adds a line about the parchment just under the still-readable clue. Desktop also shows interaction acknowledgement in the footer. On mobile the footer begins below the visible action body and falls below the fold after inspection, but the local inspection response is visible. The close control receives a clear gold outline on open; Choose and Inspect acquire focus in turn; the Journal Lens control is outlined after close. The underlying Journal returns to Follow the lanterns and the current-objective/Continue Voyage bar. Desktop normal Lens loads through an explicit opening state, around 8.78 to 9.03 seconds within that trace, and returns by 11.11 seconds. Both normal Journal returns display the animated-opening recovery notice, while reduced shows the readable fallback. The mobile book and dialog keep their core actions within the narrow width, with vertical wrapping. The reduced mobile entry briefly shows an empty page/surface before the checkpoint.
- Desktop companion shell. All six ready, library and returned PNGs and 28 normal and 26 reduced main-page trace JPEGs. The initial device settings path goes to checking access, then the Chronicle purpose, then the Journal purpose. Its header keeps Voyagewright Player and an account chip, with a shell Return, a labeled Exit to My Voyages, and the contextual Return to Chronicle. The in-sync status, release selector, A/A+ and parchment make its reading purpose clear. Exit reaches a focused My Chronicle Library heading with server-confirmed status, desktop public navigation, My Voyages, account, filters and one active voyage. Tab movement through filter controls is visible. The same active Voyage reopens with the Open the journal gate and then Follow the lanterns and Continue Voyage. Normal lands lower in the book and visibly announces recovery from the opening. Reduced reaches the readable fallback with the journal header visible and shows recovery of an interrupted connection. Full-motion transition briefly layers prior screen imagery under the next view.
- Mobile companion shell. All six checkpoint PNGs and 33 normal and 25 reduced main-page trace JPEGs at 390x844. Companion shows distinct Return, Exit to My Voyages and full-width Return to Chronicle, with Voyage and sync context above a single-column readable parchment passage. The mobile Library switches to a compact menu and stacked search/state/sort controls, with its wrapped heading visibly focused. The filters put the sole active voyage card below the first fold; the trace moves through the controls and back to the same voyage. Normal reaches page four and sees Previous/Next above the fixed shelf and objective; reduced returns higher with the readable fallback, showing an interrupted-to-restored message while the passage remains present. The fixed tabs and objective take meaningful vertical space and cover lower lines at some scroll positions, but scrolling reveals the reader controls. Initial mobile companion reconnect offers Retry and settles to Same Voyage in sync. The normal opening recovery notice and reduced readable fallback are visible limitations of this browser journey.
- Eight trace screenshot sequences were decoded and visually reviewed. No standalone videos were played, and these captures cannot establish device camera, assistive technology output, physical touch ergonomics, or owner acceptance.

composition.observation: The centered navy Lens dims the desktop Journal while keeping the book and objective bar recognizable. At 390 pixels the same bounded overlay fills most of the viewport.

typography.observation: Serif scene and note titles distinguish the story from the sans-serif availability copy and action labels. The full clue wraps legibly across three lines at the mobile checkpoint.

spacing.observation: Desktop action buttons sit on one row. Mobile wraps Place in Guided View beneath Choose and Inspect. The note and local inspection response have padding and a divider, while secondary footer text extends below the visible crop.

controls.observation: Choose, Inspect and Place in Guided View sit beside the clue, with a separate close button and a visibly disabled Start browser AR. Inspect changes the note area in the captured journey.

contrast.observation: The warm parchment carries dark clue text. Action buttons use light-on-navy lettering, and the high-contrast gold focus ring remains distinct from the dimmed page and subdued disabled AR control.

consistency.observation: Both widths and motion modes repeat the Voyage name, exact northern-light clue, action order and local inspection copy. The same objective remains visible after close.

states.observation: Journal tools appear before launch. Lens supplies an opening message, resolves to the released note, adds the inspection sentence and removes the overlay on return.

responsive.observation: Desktop keeps a centered modal and spread. Mobile shows a single Journal page and stacks the parchment controls inside the modal. Close, clue and inspection feedback are within the 390-pixel evidence.

keyboard.observation: Sampled frames show the close button focused at entry and focus moving to Choose or Inspect. The keyboard journey opens, inspects and closes while retaining the Journal content.

focus.observation: The gold ring is visible on the close control when Lens opens and on Open Chronicle Lens or Lens once the dialog closes on both widths.

feedback.observation: Inspect adds an immediate description of the parchment in all variants, and desktop also exposes the recorded-interaction footer. The captured first visible feedback measures about 104 to 211 ms.

motion.observation: Normal Journal entry animates and then shows an opening recovery notice. Reduced uses the readable page-turn fallback. Both traces present the same stable clue, inspection and direct close destination within the interaction budget.

continuity.observation: The Voyage title persists on the dialog and Follow the lanterns is present before and after. Capture continuity reports matching Voyage and edition fingerprints at the visible outcomes and after return for all four variants.

complexity.observation: The single dialog gives the clue without another setup step. The three verbs share one note panel and the visibly explained camera restriction has no effect on inspecting or returning.

role-outcomes.observation: The signed-in Player receives the released text and gets a meaningful inspection result while the returned objective remains Follow the lanterns. The capture's role and return checks pass for every reviewed mode.

fallbacks.observation: The disabled browser AR button explains that world tracking is unavailable here, while Guided View supplies the northern-light clue without a camera. Reduced Journal rendering still provides the passage and Continue Voyage.

findings.observation: The mobile Lens footer starts low and desktop's recorded-interaction footer is below the visible mobile inspected view. The parchment immediately displays its own inspection result and close remains visible.
Full-motion Journal frames explicitly report that the animated opening could not finish. The actual passage, Lens entry and return remain available.
